text.en:
On a school trip Isha travelled from the snowy Himalayas down to the Ganga plains and finally to the sea coast at Kanyakumari.
"India has so many kinds of land," she wrote in her diary. "Each place has its own life."

India has great variety in its land. The main physical regions are the Northern Mountains (the Himalayas), the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Thar Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands.
The Himalayas are young fold mountains with snow-covered peaks and the source of rivers such as the Ganga. The Northern Plains are fertile and densely populated. The Peninsular Plateau is old and rich in minerals. The Thar Desert in the west is dry.
The coastal plains lie along the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, and the islands include Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Landscape affects farming, houses, jobs and way of life.
India has mountains, plains, a plateau, a desert, coasts and islands.
The Himalayas are young mountains and the source of great rivers.
The Northern Plains are fertile and crowded. The Peninsular Plateau is old and rich in minerals.
Landscape shapes farming, houses and jobs.

problem.en: Why is the Northern Plain so thickly populated?

text.en: The land is flat, so roads and towns are easy to build.
So many people live and work here.

prompt.en: A friend says India has only mountains and plains. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: India also has a plateau, a desert, coasts and islands.
Each region has its own life.

points.en: India's regions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Thar Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.
Northern Plains are fertile and crowded.
